feat: run the SuperMimic learner on MPS for the MuJoCo host bridge on macOS

commit.message:
feat: run the SuperMimic learner on MPS for the MuJoCo host bridge on macOS

On macOS the MuJoCo HOST_BRIDGE backend keeps env tensors on CPU, which
previously pinned the whole learner to CPU fp32: the hard-coded
autocast("cuda") in run_mlp was silently disabled, TF32 flags were
inert, and torch.compile's inductor Metal codegen crashed outright.

- run_mlp now autocasts on the input tensor's device (cuda/mps), so
  bf16 AMP actually applies on Apple Silicon; CUDA/ROCm behavior is
  unchanged.
- SuperMimicLearner accepts an explicit device and, only when it
  differs from the env device, bridges tensors at the env boundary and
  trains on its own MDP copy (new MDP/MotionLib/G1Kinematics.to()
  return moved shallow copies). Matching devices keep the exact old
  code path, so CUDA/ROCm runs are unaffected.
- torch.compile falls back to backend="aot_eager" on MPS because
  inductor has no working Metal codegen there.

Same short-run config (MuJoCo backend, 512 envs x 60 iters, M5 Max):
0.050 -> 0.712 it/s (~14x), GPU utilization ~0% -> ~90%, with matching
loss/reward curves.

commit.message:
feat: replace OffPolicyLogger reuse with SuperMimic-adapted training logger

Directly reusing unilab's OffPolicyLogger does not fit: its metric schema
is a closed set of generic names (Loss/aux_*, Loss/surrogate, ...), so
SuperMimic's real metrics (wm_loss, imag_rew, term_frac, ...) were being
reported under names that do not match.

Add unisupermimic.rl.logging.SuperMimicLogger, adapted from the upstream
unilab/rl/logging/offpolicy.py (Apache-2.0, attribution in the file
header), keeping the parts that apply and dropping distributed ranks,
async collector/replay timing, wandb, and the schema validation:

- Rich live panel at 1 Hz: iteration x/N progress bar, elapsed/ETA,
  it/s and sim steps/s, a metrics table with the real names (wm_loss,
  wm_err8, pi_loss, v_loss, imag_rew, imag_survival, pi_gradnorm, lr),
  a sim_rew sparkline with mean/peak, episode stats (ep_len, ep_ret_norm,
  term_frac), and per-iteration collect/learn/total timing.
- TensorBoard backend writing the real metric names (Loss/world_model,
  Loss/policy, Reward/sim_step_norm, Episode/length, Perf/it_per_s, ...).
  algo.log_backend=none disables TB, =no_print silences everything
  (used by the CPU learner tests).
- Warmup buffer-fill progress, one-off torch.compile status messages,
  checkpoint save notices, and a training summary on completion.
- Non-TTY output stays quiet: status lines only, final panel and summary
  printed once at the end.

train_log.csv logging is unchanged and remains the authoritative record.
FakeEnv test transitions gain the term/ep_len/ep_ret_norm contract fields
so the episode-metric path is exercised, with new tests asserting the TB
scalar names and that no_print writes no events.

feat: add UniLab OffPolicyLogger progress dashboard to SuperMimic training

SuperMimic training previously printed nothing during a run; the only
progress signal was tailing train_log.csv. Reuse unilab's
unilab.rl.logging.offpolicy.OffPolicyLogger (same logger UniLab's
off-policy algorithms use) instead of writing a local clone:

  record. algo.log_backend=none disables TB, =no_print silences
  everything (used by the CPU learner tests).
- Buffer-fill / collector counters before the loop, compile status
  messages during the one-off torch.compile warmup, and checkpoint
  save notifications.

Metric names are mapped onto unilab's closed metric schema
(Loss/aux_* prefix, Loss/surrogate, Loss/value, Loss/learning_rate,
Train/actor_gradient_norm, reward/* open prefix).

Merge pull request #3 from Motphys/fix/rocm-tf32-misaligned-bmm

fix: enable TF32 only for fp32 training to unblock ROCm host-bridge

commit.message:
fix: enable TF32 only for fp32 training to unblock ROCm host-bridge

On ROCm, a TF32 bmm over the misaligned strided views produced by
unflatten_state (e.g. lin_vel at a 28-byte storage offset) triggers
per-call rocBLAS kernel selection costing ~100-170 ms per call. The
eager collect() path issues dozens of these tiny fp32 geometry bmms per
environment step, so mujoco/motrix host-bridge training on MI300X ran
at ~0.27 it/s with the GPU idle.

TF32 never helped the default bf16 path in the first place: every heavy
GEMM already runs in bf16 through autocast. Gate the flag on
amp == 'none' so fp32 training keeps TF32 on CUDA while the default
path no longer trips the rocBLAS pathology.

Measured on MI300X (mujoco backend, 4096 envs): mdp.obs 173 ms ->
0.11 ms, wm.inputs 349 ms -> 0.19 ms, wm.targets 521 ms -> 0.97 ms per
call. NVIDIA throughput unchanged.

Merge pull request #2 from Motphys/fix/host-bridge-collector-tensor-device

fix: route host-bridge collector tensors to the learner device

commit.message:
fix: route host-bridge collector tensors to the learner device

MuJoCo and Motrix are HOST_BRIDGE backends: physics steps on the host,
and unilab defaults the manager carrier to CPU unless the caller routes
training.collector_tensor_device. SuperMimic's learner inherits
env.device, so training with task=g1_super_mimic/mujoco placed the
entire world model, policy, and replay buffer on CPU -- a single
wm_update backward took minutes, making training appear hung.

Adopt unilab's owner-layer mechanism instead of a local workaround:
build_env_override now applies apply_collector_tensor_device_override
with select_collector_tensor_device(cfg) and the resolved learner
device, matching train_appo/train_rsl_rl. The new
training.collector_tensor_device owner key defaults to auto: a CUDA
learner (including ROCm/HIP's cuda namespace) routes the indexed
learner device, a CPU learner routes CPU, and mjwarp is untouched
(device-resident). Explicit cpu with a CUDA learner keeps failing
closed on non-ROCm builds per unilab issue #2483. The resolved device
is recorded in run_config.json via
resolve_recorded_collector_tensor_device.

Validated with unilab 1.5.0 (pinned by both uv.lock and uv.rocm.lock):
uv run unisupermimic-train task=g1_super_mimic/mujoco now trains at
~4 it/s with the GPU at ~78% (previously no log row ever appeared).
pytest -m '' 83 passed; ruff, mypy, pyright clean.

commit.message:
feat: add ROCm dependency profile for AMD GPU training

Add pyproject.rocm.toml + uv.rocm.lock (profile swap) so ROCm hosts
install a ROCm PyTorch build via make sync-rocm, with make sync-default
to return to the default profile and make lock-rocm for maintainers to
regenerate the ROCm lockfile.

The ROCm lock is identical to the default lock except for the
torch==2.14.1+rocm7.2 fork and triton-rocm==3.8.0: torch/triton-rocm
are direct requirements pinned to the explicit pytorch-rocm72 index
(uv applies tool.uv.sources to direct dependencies only), which keeps
stale pytorch-index mirrors of unrelated packages out of the lock.

Verified end-to-end on an MI300X host: uv sync --locked installs
torch 2.14.1+rocm7.2 (hip 7.2.53211) with CUDA API available, and
unisupermimic/unilab import cleanly. CUDA-only backends (mjwarp)
remain unsupported on ROCm; training uses the MuJoCo host-bridge
backend (task=g1_super_mimic/mujoco).
